turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, hi. I'm here because... well, I just can't stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. It's really getting to me. Like, I feel like everyone at the warehouse is noticing it, or even if I go out to salsa night, I just know people are staring at it. People tell me they don't see anything when I bring it up, but... I just can't stop focusing on it. It's pretty much all I think about.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation with a perceived flaw on the left side of their face that others report not seeing.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel anxious or extremely self-conscious in social situations, especially because of your appearance?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, definitely. I get extremely self-conscious about it. It's actually getting to the point where it's really messing up my life. I've even been written up at the warehouse recently because my work keeps getting delayed... I just get too caught up worrying about it while I'm trying to pull orders. 

And socially, yeah, I've just started skipping things. I don't go to my soccer games anymore, or those salsa nights I mentioned. I even skip family gatherings now. I just... I really don't want to deal with people looking at me, or having to be in any pictures. It's just easier to stay home.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms being extremely self-conscious about their appearance and describes persistent preoccupation, stating they get too caught up worrying about it to the point of workplace delays and social avoidance.

turns.doctor_question: How much time per day would you say you spend thinking about the way your face looks, and does it interfere with your ability to focus on other things?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not exactly sure how many hours it is, to be honest. It feels like... well, pretty much all day. From the time I wake up until I go to sleep, it's just always there in my head. 

And yeah, it definitely wrecks my focus. Like I was saying about getting written up at the warehouse, I'll be in the middle of pulling an order and just completely lose track of what I'm doing because I'm so stuck worrying about how crooked my face looks. It makes it really hard to concentrate on anything else.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an all-day preoccupation with the belief that their face is crooked, noting it is constantly in their head and disrupts daily functioning.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any days in the past two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies loss of interest, stating they definitely still have interest and want to engage in activities they enjoy like soccer and salsa.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix how it looks in any way?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always stop in the bathroom to check my face in the mirror. I end up just standing there, fixing my cap and rubbing at the same spot on my face over and over. I get so caught up doing it that I end up being late getting back to the floor. That's actually why my picking numbers keep falling behind and my boss keeps getting on me.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors regarding appearance, specifically repeatedly checking the mirror, adjusting their cap, and rubbing the same spot on their face to the point of causing occupational impairment.

turns.doctor_question: When you're worried about your face looking crooked, is your main concern that it looks physically deformed or unattractive, even if others don't see it that way?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's exactly it. I just can't stop thinking that the left side of my face looks completely crooked and... well, just messed up. 

To me, it looks deformed, and I feel like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is staring at it and noticing it. And the thing is, even when people tell me they don't see anything wrong, or that they don't know what I'm talking about, it doesn't really matter. I just can't believe them. I still see it, and I'm still convinced everyone else does too.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient explicitly confirms a persistent preoccupation with a perceived facial asymmetry and deformity that others repeatedly state they do not see.
